When you replace the `dist/` folder, env vars set only in the shell session disappear. The app **will not crash** without them (it falls back gracefully), but `MONGODB_URI` missing means it uses in-memory storage — which could cause errors.

**Why the server was hanging on startup**
The `migrateLegacyProfiles` function was running synchronously on boot — fetching and updating all 57K users before the server could start listening. Fixed by running it in the background so the server starts immediately.

**Why `/api/anglers` was returning a 500 error**
MongoDB Atlas free tier caps in-memory sort operations at 32MB. With 57K anglers, the sort query blew past that. Fixed by adding `allowDiskUse: true` to the aggregation pipeline, which lets MongoDB spill to disk for large sorts.

**Why the admin dashboard took 20+ seconds**
It was loading all 57K users just to count them. Fixed with a single `countDocuments()` call instead.

**Why recent participations took 24+ seconds**
It loaded every single participation record + all 57K users just to show 10 rows. Fixed to fetch only the 10 most recent participants via a MongoDB sort+limit, then do 10 fast indexed lookups for names.

**Why admin anglers took 21+ seconds (and would crash the browser)**
Same problem — loading all 57K users. Fixed with server-side pagination (50 per page) and server-side search. The admin Anglers page now has pagination controls and real-time search that queries the server instead of filtering 57K rows in the browser.

**Assign Peg / Add Angler dialogs**
Both dialogs used to load all 57K anglers into a dropdown. Now they show a search box — type a name and it fetches matching anglers from the server (max 30 results).

**With the current query, here's who gets deleted vs kept:**

| Real user, active (verified email), no competitions yet | `active` | ✅ **Safe — KEPT** |
| Real user, registered but never verified email | `pending` | ⚠️ **Would be deleted** |
| Spam bot | `pending` | ✅ Deleted (correct) |

So the only risky case is someone who registered, **never clicked the verification link**, and also never entered a competition. In practice most real users do one or both — but to be safe, here's an improved version:

**Safer cleanup — also excludes recently registered accounts:**

```javascript
// Keep anyone who registered in the last 30 days (give real users benefit of the doubt)
const thirtyDaysAgo = new Date()
thirtyDaysAgo.setDate(thirtyDaysAgo.getDate() - 30)

const participantIds = db.competition_participants.distinct("userId")
const paymentIds = db.payments.distinct("userId")
const realUserIds = [...new Set([...participantIds, ...paymentIds])]

// Preview count first (safe, read-only)
db.users.countDocuments({
  id: { $nin: realUserIds },
  status: "pending",
  createdAt: { $lt: thirtyDaysAgo }  // only accounts older than 30 days
})

// Then delete when you're happy with the number
db.users.deleteMany({
  id: { $nin: realUserIds },
  status: "pending",
  createdAt: { $lt: thirtyDaysAgo }
})
```

This version protects:
- ✅ Anyone who verified their email (status `active`)
- ✅ Anyone who joined or paid for a competition
- ✅ Anyone who registered in the last 30 days (even if not yet verified)

The only accounts deleted are ones that are **older than 30 days**, still unverified, and have never touched a competition — almost certainly bots.
